title: Microglia replacement by bone marrow transplantation (Mr BMT) in the central nervous system of adult mice
protocol: Administer PLX5622-formulated diet for two weeks.
Apply 9 Gy whole-body irradiation.
Perform bone marrow transplantation immediately after irradiation.
Replace PLX5622-formulated diet with control diet for 30 days.
Treat the mouse with neomycin (1.1 g/L) containing acid water (pH 2 to 3) ad libitum from D11 to D28.
Change the PLX5622-formulated chow with sterilized AIN-76A control diet (CD) 2–3 hours before lethal irradiation at D14.
Cut a piece of sterilized foam plastic pad to fit into an open mouse cage.
Place the recipient mice in an open cage.
Cover the cage with the foam plastic piece and press down so that mice can only crawl on the floor.
Set the irradiation dosage to 9 Gy on the X-ray irradiator (Radsource, RS-2000).
Put the mouse cage in the irradiator and initiate irradiation.
Remove the covering foam plastic piece from the cage after irradiation.
Feed the irradiated mouse with sterilized CD and neomycin containing acid water (1.1 g/L, pH 2 to 3) ad libitum.
Anesthetize the CX3CR1+/GFP donor mouse deeply with ketamine (100 mg/kg) and xylazine (10 mg/kg) by intraperitoneal injection.
Dislocate the cervical spine of the donor mouse after loss of the toe reflex.
Isolate the femurs, tibias, and humerus from the donor mouse.
Clean up soft tissues from the bones with Kim Wipes.
Place the cleaned bones in a dish containing ice cold PBS.
Wash the bones three times to remove attached soft tissue and furs.
Isolate femurs, tibias, and humerus.
Cut off both ends of the bones.
Fill a 5 mL syringe with ice cold PBS using a 21 G needle.
Insert the needle into one end of the bone.
Flush out the bone marrow into the cell strainer.
Repeat flushing until all bones are processed.
Triturate the bone marrow piece with a 1 mL pipette for 10 times.
Pour the triturated bone marrow cells into the cell strainer.
Grind remaining bone marrow against the strainer with the plunger from the syringe until no obvious pieces remain.
Wash the strainer with 2 mL ice cold PBS.
Centrifuge at 4°C at 300 g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Add 1 mL ACK lysis buffer at room temperature (approximately 20°C–25°C) for 1 min.
Add 9 mL ice cold PBS to the cell suspension and mix gently.
Centrifuge at 4°C 300 g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellets with appropriate amount of PBS (550 μL per donor mice).
Count the total cell numbers in the central grid and grids of the four corners using hemacytometers.
Calculate the average cell number.
Multiply the average cell number by 104 to estimate the number of cells per microliter.
Place the C57BL/6J recipient mouse into the restraining tube carefully.
Insert face-mask plug into the restraining tube so that the mouse cannot move but can still breathe easily.
Tighten the screw on the plug.
Aspire 100 μL donor cells into a 29 G syringe without trapped bubbles.
Straighten the tail of the mouse.
Locate the tail vein about 2 cm from tail tips as the injection site with the help of an orange LED light placed beneath the tail.
Choose the most accessible side tail vein for injection.
Insert half of the needle bevel into the injection site at an angle of about 30° to the tail, then insert about 1 mm of the needle parallelly into the tail vein.
Slowly inject the cells into the vein.
Press the injection site and withdraw the needle.
Keep pressing the injection site while releasing the mouse from the restrainer with the mouse tail still in hand.
After releasing the mice, press the injection site for another 20 seconds.
Feed the transplanted mouse ad libitum with sterilized CD for recovery of 30 days.
Treat the mouse with neomycin-containing acid water (1.1 g/L, pH 2 to 3) for the first 2–3 weeks after transplantation.
